title: The Personal Archive as Succession Infrastructure
author: RN Collins
rightsRule: Evidence leads; atmosphere never substitutes for provenance.

carouselA.title: The Personal Archive as Succession Infrastructure: the institutional sequence

frames.caption: A personal archive becomes succession infrastructure when it preserves not only the work, but the founder’s decision logic, rights evidence, relationships, access pathways, and instructions for future interpretation.
frames.alt: Title plate for The Personal Archive as Succession Infrastructure.
frames.treatment: typography, rule, folio and domain color only

frames.caption: An accession-quality record preserves a house object beyond the founder’s lifetime while keeping the object, maker attribution, and museum stewardship distinct.
frames.credit: Gift of James A. and Mary Elizabeth Kingsland, 1994
frames.alt: Elaborate House of Worth silk fancy dress costume with a fitted bodice, dark patterned skirt, and dramatic decorative sleeves, around 1893.

frames.crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
frames.caption: 01 · CAPTURE — What cannot be reconstructed later?. Record why a choice was made, who contributed, what failed, what remains sensitive, and which relationship holds tacit knowledge. Use audio when voice carries nuance the file cannot.
frames.credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
frames.alt: Diagram mapping what cannot be reconstructed later? within The Personal Archive as Succession Infrastructure.
frames.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery
frames.treatment: render from verified text, source IDs, lines and geometric fields

frames.crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
frames.caption: 02 · PAIR — Can the physical and digital records find one another?. Pair garments, samples, notebooks, photographs, contracts, communications, and born-digital files through stable identifiers and relationship fields.
frames.credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
frames.alt: Diagram mapping can the physical and digital records find one another? within The Personal Archive as Succession Infrastructure.
frames.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery
frames.treatment: render from verified text, source IDs, lines and geometric fields

frames.crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
frames.caption: 03 · PRESERVE — Will the record open and remain trustworthy?. Maintain master and backup copies, record checksums and formats, document transformations, migrate deliberately, and keep known gaps visible.
frames.credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
frames.alt: Diagram mapping will the record open and remain trustworthy? within The Personal Archive as Succession Infrastructure.
frames.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery
frames.treatment: render from verified text, source IDs, lines and geometric fields

frames.crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
frames.caption: 04 · AUTHORIZE — Who may act after absence?. Name stewards, alternates, access rules, privacy limits, conservation referrals, legal instruments, and a review process for loans, publication, licensing, interpretation, and disposal.
frames.credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
frames.alt: Diagram mapping who may act after absence? within The Personal Archive as Succession Infrastructure.
frames.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery
frames.treatment: render from verified text, source IDs, lines and geometric fields

frames.caption: A total archive can become surveillance of the founder, collaborators, family, workers, and communities. Preservation is not a command to keep or publish everything. Appraisal, consent, privacy, embargo, deletion, and culturally appropriate restriction belong inside succession design.
frames.alt: Counterpoint card for The Personal Archive as Succession Infrastructure.
frames.treatment: typographic quotation field; no decorative imagery
